chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa’ed Abady, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of his father who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said:
Five things are impossible from five: good advice from a jealous person; mercy from an enemy; sanctity from a corrupt person; loyalty from a woman; and grandeur from a poor person.

key_terms.الْفَاسِقُ: The corrupt/sinner (one who transgresses religious bounds)

ai.seo_question: What are the five things considered impossible or incompatible with specific types of people according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines five natural incompatibilities, reflecting the Shia scholarly understanding of *fitrah* (innate nature) and social dynamics. While 'loyalty from a woman' is often interpreted as referring to the general disposition of women in that context rather than a universal absolute, the other four highlight how internal states like envy or poverty inherently limit external expressions like sincerity or awe. This enumeration serves as a practical guide for believers to assess character and expectations in interpersonal relationships.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 5-5 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa’ed Abady, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy, on the authority of his father who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “
Five things are impossible from five: good advice from a jealous person; mercy from an enemy; sanctity from a corrupt person; loyalty from a woman; and grandeur from a poor person.”
